title: KV Rebalance Controller: background compaction & fragmentation mitigation
creator: Jordan Kaplan
description:
Problem: Long-running inference servers accumulate fragmented KV cache allocations (many small free holes and scattered cold entries). This increases allocation latency for new KV slots, forces premature evictions, and reduces usable GPU RAM by up to double-digit percentages under adversarial workloads. Existing work focuses on slab and buddy allocators; this ticket proposes a runtime-level KV Rebalance Controller that reduces fragmentation without requiring a global stop-the-world GC or invasive allocator rewrite.

Proposal: Implement a cooperative background compaction and rebalance controller with three coordinated mechanisms: 1) Hot-cold migration: identify cold KV entries based on access recency and migrate them into coalesced target segments to free contiguous ranges; 2) Segment-level consolidation: maintain lightweight per-GPU segment maps and a background task that compacts free ranges by copying live entries to destination segments during low-util windows; 3) Allocation advisory + batching integration: surface a fragmentation score to the continuous batching scheduler so it can prefer GPUs/instances with lower fragmentation for latency-sensitive batches and schedule rebalance work during non-critical windows.

Key design points: no global pause - compaction runs as an incremental job that copies small groups of KV entries and updates metadata atomically via epoched pointers and version tags; support pinned entries (pinned by in-flight batches) by skipping and including them in subsequent passes; use a small write-ahead metadata journal per-GPU to recover if crash occurs during migration; heuristics to trigger compaction (fragmentation > 12% wasted bytes OR allocation slowpath hit rate > 0.5% for 1 minute).

Trade-offs: compaction reduces fragmentation at the cost of additional GPU memory copies and transient extra memory for destination buffers. We will cap compaction throughput to limit impact on live inference (default 10% of GPU bandwidth) and offer a strict mode for Dedicated that pauses compaction during SLO breaches. Cross-model migrations handled conservatively to avoid model isolation violations in Private deployments; for Private we require admin opt-in for cross-model segment sharing.

Spike results: initial prototype (spike-compact branch) on an A100 testbed reduced fragmentation from 18% to 3% on a synthetic broken-allocation workload and reduced allocation slowpath latencies by 60% at peak. However, end-to-end tail latency for 99th percentile microbench increased by ~3ms during compaction spikes; we will mitigate via scheduling and bandwidth capping.

Acceptance criteria: listed below.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype compaction can reduce measured fragmentation to <6% on three synthetic workloads (mixed-length, adversarial-churn, long-tail growth)
Allocation slowpath rate reduced by >=40% under representative production load in staging
No increase in 99.9th percentile token latency >5ms attributable to compaction when capped to default bandwidth limits
Durability: after simulated GPU crash during compaction, metadata journal allows correct recovery with no KV corruption
Integration: batching scheduler receives fragmentation score and prefers lower-fragmentation hosts in at least one A/B rollout

implementation_notes: Phase 1: Instrumentation + fragmentation scoring (2 points) - expose per-segment free-run histograms and allocation slowpath counters; integrate score to scheduler.
Phase 2: Background copier + metadata journal (3 points) - implement incremental copy loop, epoched pointer swap, circular WAL, and recovery routine.
Phase 3: Safety + policies (2 points) - bandwidth cap, strict-mode, admin opt-in for cross-model consolidation, telemetry dashboards and alerts.
Phase 4: Rollout (1 point) - canary on low-impact regions, A/B test scheduler integration, and runtime config for Dedicated customers.
